sanskrit: sarvathā divasāntarāṣṭyatikramya paurṇamāsyāṃtāvat kṛtaṃ karma tāvanmātraṃ ca śāstreṇītaṃ na vyāpti, ritaratra punarjīvitavyatirikta kākāsaṃbhavāyavacchedyaṃ na kiṃ cidastīti vyatāvasatyāṃ samastameva vākyamanarthakaṃ syāt /
english: That is to say, in the case of the Paurnamasi, it does not matter if the whole day is not filled up because there are reasons for this, in the shape of the brevity of the sacrificial process, and in that of the distinct Injunction that the sacrifice is to be performed in the morning. Conse quently, in that case, inasmuch as the sacrifice will have been performed on the Paurnamāsī day, and on no other,the Injunction will have been duly fulfilled as that is all that is meant by the Injunction, which says nothing as to the filling up of the whole day by the performance. In the for the performer, apart from his lifetime and as such there is no time that could be taken as precluded by the word lifetime conse quently if the time prescribed were not duly filled up, the whole sentence would become meaningless.
